'''Manuel Sanchís Hontiyuelo''' ({{IPA|es|maˈnolo sanˈtʃis}}; born 23 May 1965) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[sweeper (association football)|sweeper]].

A part of the famous ''[[La Quinta del Buitre]]'' which stemmed from the [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] youth academy, he was the only one of its five members to spend his [[List of one-club men in association football|entire career]] with the club. His father [[Manuel Sanchís]] also played for Real Madrid, and both were [[Spain national football team|Spanish internationals]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20090529/los-busquets-hacen-historia_53711968607.html|title=Los Busquets hacen historia|trans-title=The Busquets make history|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=29 May 2009|access-date=8 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/blogs/deportes/libredirecto/2013/03/23/la-quinta-entra-en-los-50.html|title=La Quinta entra en los 50|trans-title=The Cohort hits 50|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Orfeo|last=Suárez|language=es|date=23 March 2013|access-date=5 October 2019}}</ref>

Sanchís appeared in more than 700 competitive matches for his only club, and represented the national team in one [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] and one [[UEFA European Championship|European Championship]].

==Club career==
A product of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s prolific youth system, [[Madrid]]-born Sanchís made his debut with the first team on 4 December 1983, scoring the only goal at [[Real Murcia CF]] and finishing his [[1983–84 La Liga|debut campaign]] with a further 17 appearances (and two goals) for the main squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2008/12/05/mas_futbol/1228462063_850215.html|title="Cambiamos la ideología del fútbol español"|trans-title="We changed the ideology of Spanish football"|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Enrique|last=Ortego|language=es|date=5 December 2008|access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref>

Sanchís only appeared in less than 30 matches in two of the following 15 seasons, and was instrumental in the team's several conquests, including six [[La Liga]] championships, two [[UEFA Champions League]]s and two [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cups]]. In [[1999–2000 La Liga|1999–2000]] he featured sparingly, but still helped them to their [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|eighth European Cup]], playing 11 minutes in [[2000 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] against fellow Spanish side [[Valencia CF]] in a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/realmadrid-in-ec.html|title=Real Madrid CF – All the players in European Cups|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first=Emilio|last=Pla Díaz|access-date=6 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/24/championsleague.sport1|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Valencia|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 May 2000|access-date=29 June 2016}}</ref>

Sanchís retired in 2001 at the age of 36, having played 710 official games for his only club – 523 of those in the league – while also [[Captain (association football)|captaining]] it for 13 years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20171207/433474069953/ramos-entra-entre-los-diez-jugadores-con-mas-partidos-con-el-real-madrid.html|title=Ramos entra entre los diez jugadores con más partidos con el Real Madrid|trans-title=Ramos joins ten players with more matches with Real Madrid|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=7 December 2017|access-date=4 June 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
After excelling with the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spanish under-21s]], with which he won the [[1986 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|1986 UEFA European Championship]],<ref name=MD>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1986/10/30/pagina-3/1144661/pdf.html|title=¡¡¡Campeones!!!|trans-title=Champions!!!|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Francesc|last=Perearnau|language=es|date=30 October 1986|access-date=5 June 2014}}</ref> Sanchís made his [[Spain national football team|senior]] debut on 12 November of that year in a [[UEFA Euro 1988]] [[UEFA Euro 1988 qualifying|qualifier]] against [[Romania national football team|Romania]] (1–0 win).<ref name=AS>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/05/01/reportajes/1588284569_032666.html|title=La 'Quinta del Buitre', de héroes a villanos|trans-title=The 'Vulture's Cohort', from heroes to villains|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Enrique|last=Ortego|language=es|date=1 May 2020|access-date=15 May 2023}}</ref> He went on to earn 48 full [[Cap (sport)|caps]], appearing at both Euro 1988 and the [[1990 FIFA World Cup]].<ref name=AS/>

Sanchís scored his only international goal on 14 October 1987, Spain's second in a 2–0 home victory over [[Austria national football team|Austria]] also in a Euro 1988 qualifying match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2021/05/19/reportajes/1621435397_252332.html|title=España no necesitó repetir la gesta de Malta|trans-title=Spain did not to repeat the Malta exploit|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=19 May 2021|access-date=20 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/sanchis-intl.html|title=Manuel Sanchís – International Matches|publisher=RSSSF|first=Emilio|last=Pla Díaz|access-date=9 September 2025}}</ref> His last game, aged 27, was a 2–0 [[Exhibition game#International football|friendly]] defeat of the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] on 11 March 1992.<ref name=AS/>

==Style of play==
As a [[central defender]], Sanchís stood out for his defensive composure, placement and agility. He set a new standard within his club due to both his sporting and human skills.<ref name=RM>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/about-real-madrid/history/football-legends/manuel-sanchis-hontiyuelo|title=The saga continues|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=27 November 2018}}</ref> An aggressive yet fair player,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2229937-real-madrid-vs-barcelona-all-time-clasico-40-best-players|title=Real Madrid vs. Barcelona: All-Time Clasico 40 Best Players|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Karl|last=Matchett|date=23 October 2014|access-date=21 February 2021}}</ref> he was also noted for his leadership, tactical intelligence, reading of the game and positional sense in addition to his passing, and usually played as a sweeper.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/37444243/is-sergio-ramos-leader-real-madrid-need-be|title=Is captain Sergio Ramos the on-field leader Real Madrid need him to be?|publisher=[[ESPN]]|first=Eduardo|last=Alvarez|date=31 March 2016|access-date=16 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/gallery/where-are-they-now-real-madrids-1998-champions-league-winners|title=Where are they now? Real Madrid's 1998 Champions League winners|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|first=Paul|last=Sarahs|date=24 May 2018|access-date=21 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/top-5-greatest-real-madrid-captains-of-all-time-sstl|title=Top 5 greatest Real Madrid captains of all time|publisher=Sportskeeda|first=Ninad|last=Singh|date=24 October 2018|access-date=16 June 2026}}</ref>
